success_criteria: All 37 planned files contain only the approved independent-kata build/toolchain changes.
Every one of the 12 Gradle wrapper roots reports Gradle 8.10.2 and completes clean build, which executes every included subproject.
All 22 build.gradle files use sourceCompatibility 17; no active jcenter(), compile, or testCompile declaration remains.
Requested Java dependency versions are present and Mockito/Guava consumers pass tests.
Existing kata suites provide the smoke and integration coverage for this build-only upgrade; no generated test file or cross-kata test harness is required.
npm install succeeds under Node 22 and the regenerated package-lock.json matches package.json.
Both npm run test:jest and npm run test:mocha pass; rimraf cleanup succeeds with --glob; Chai remains major 4.
No external service, datastore, startup/browser, or cross-kata coupling is introduced.

rollback_strategy: Revert the single final execution commit created by the executor.
planning_notes: All 37 changes come directly from the ImpactReport. Targeted line ranges were sufficient except package.json and the short representative build files algorithm/dijkstra/build.gradle, refactoring/chartsmart/java/build.gradle, refactoring/trivia/java/build.gradle, and tdd/stringcalculator/java/build.gradle, which were read in full to verify literal formatting and unambiguous Gradle 8 replacements. The user supplied exact npm commands; they are preserved. The user described Gradle validation as a coverage requirement rather than exact commands, so `.\gradlew.bat clean build --no-daemon` is inferred for each of the 12 wrapper roots; `build` includes tests and automatically covers all settings.gradle subprojects. npm install is repeated in final build validation because the final schema has no setup-command list. There are no startup commands, pages, flows, databases, search indexes, brokers, or external services. A scope expansion budget of 3 files is pre-authorized only for an unplanned file whose bounded build/test failure is a direct call into one of the already approved major-version upgrades; it does not authorize cross-kata edits, unrelated fixes, new dependencies, or refactors. Exact npm patch selections are deterministic members of the user-requested caret lines.
